history.dynasty: Chalukya/Rashtrakuta-era (7th century per travel sources — verify); relocated and reconstructed in modern times
history.period: 7th century (traditional dating, unverified); relocation to hilltop modern
history.summary: The Rupala (Roopala) Sangameswara Swamy Temple on Jagannatha Gattu, a small hill adjoining Kurnool town (B. Thandrapadu/Dinnedevarapadu). It is an ancient Shiva shrine with a ~6-ft granite linga that legend says was brought from Kashi by Bhima of the Pandavas; the temple was relocated stone-by-stone to the hilltop and reconstructed using historic stone blocks, and the hill gained prominence from this relocation. An Abhayanjaneya (Hanuman) idol stands nearby and the hilltop offers panoramic views of Kurnool city. The AP archaeology protected-monuments list for Kurnool includes 'Sri Jagannathagutta cave temple'. VERIFY: original dating is uncertain — sources say 7th century Chalukya or Rashtrakuta era without citation.

name: Jagannatha Gattu Temple
town_description: Kurnool, on the banks of the Tungabhadra in western Andhra Pradesh, is one of the oldest cities of the region — a former capital of Andhra State (1953-1956). It is a pilgrimage hub ringed by major shrines: the Jagannatha Gattu hill temples, Mahanandi, Ahobilam, Srisailam and Mantralayam are all within reach, and the Kondareddy Buruju fort tower stands in the old town.

travel.railway: Kurnool City railway station (nearest major railhead)
travel.road: Jagannatha Gattu hill, B. Thandrapadu, on the Kurnool-Nandyal road near G. Pulla Reddy Engineering College; ghat road to the hilltop

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; sunrise/sunset for the panoramic city views; Maha Shivaratri
